newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes lower as cold retreats.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes lower as cold retreats.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended a slow session lower as temperatures in the western U.S. retreated to more moderate levels, trade sources said Friday.
They also cited the coming Christmas holiday and next week's expiration of January contracts as limiting trading interest.
Physical market prices were also lower after soaring sharply higher early in the week in reaction to freezing temperatures in the Northwest, which have now eased.
Traders noted natural gas prices continue to play a big role in NYMEX electricity, despite signals that hydroelectric power supplies are likely to remain above normal in coming months.
But the markets have become somewhat de-coupled over the last two trading sessions, with NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas gaining 16.4 cents Friday to close at $4.573 per million British thermal units.
January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures ended down 1 cent at $26.85 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the February contract was down 29 cents at $20.10.
Other active COB contracts were 10 to 35 cents lower.
January Palo Verde was down 22 cents at $27.68, while February lost 20 cents to close at $21.75 per MWh.
Other PV contracts closed fell 20 to 25 cents.
